entries.description: A stranger on the road: attitude, ancestry, occupation
How they carry themselves (with the article)
Ancestry, weighted towards the common folk of the roads
What they do for a living
Why they need help (a full sentence)

rows.text: Their mule has gone lame a day short of market.
A wheel has come off their cart, and the load is too heavy to lift alone.
They lost the road in the fog, and their lamp oil is gone.
Their companion has a fever and is getting worse.
Wolves scattered their flock in the night.
They were robbed at the last crossing and have nothing left for the toll.

entries.description: What happens if nobody helps (a full sentence)

rows.text: If they miss the market, the family goes hungry this winter.
A wedding is waiting for them in the next town.
The letters they carry are due at the magistrate's by tomorrow.
They owe money to people who don't wait.
Their child is waiting for them alone at home.

entries.description: Something that makes a confrontation worse (a full sentence)

rows.text: Rain has turned the road to sucking mud.
The road narrows between steep banks here.
One of them is barely more than a child.
Your pack mule is skittish and close to bolting.
